THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORAL JUDGMENT

Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties,
they are taken up for final disposal.

2. These appeals are arising out of the judgment and award dated 01.06.2018 passed in MVC No.2839/2016 on the file of the XII Addl. District & Sessions Judge & MACT-XIII, Belagavi sitting at Gokak (for short, 'Tribunal')
3. MFA No.103090/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the liability and MFA No.104542/2018 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.
4.

entities.text: XII Addl. District & Sessions Judge & MACT-XIII, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts leading to filing these appeals are that on 05.07.2015 Kumar Sheetal was proceeding as a pillion rider along with Sandeep S/o. Bharmappa NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 Hosamani on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 49/Q-6847 from Nagannur to Savadi, at that time,
respondent No.1, driver-cum-owner of Mahindra pickup vehicle bearing registration No.KA-28/A-1971 came in rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motorcycle, resultantly the pillion rider fell down, sustained grievous injuries, latter he succumbed to the injuries.
It is averred that the deceased was a minor, aged about 15 years and was studying in 9th Standard.
It is submitted that the deceased used to help the family members in agricultural activities and used to contribute to the extent of Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence, the claim petition is filed for the accidental death of Kumar Sheetal.
5. Respondents entered appearance before the Tribunal and opposed the claim petition by denying liability, age, income and avocation of the deceased and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

6. The Tribunal on appreciation of evidence available on record awarded total compensation of NC:
2024:KHC-D:11463 Rs.6,15,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the same, these appeals have been filed.
Shri.Sudhakar S/O. Satappa Hosamani vs Shri Mahesh S/O. Adiveppa Gondali on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80674056/

3 7. Sri. Rajashekhar Arani, learned counsel appearing for appellant-Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in saddling the entire liability on the appellant-Insurance Company holding that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent without appreciating the fact that the eyewitness PW2 in his cross-examination has admitted that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

It is submitted that MVI Report at Ex.P7 indicates that no visual damage is caused to the offending vehicle which is another factor leading to the conclusion that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent, hence, some liability ought to have been fastened on the rider of the motorcycle.

He further submits that the Tribunal taking note of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Kishan Gopal and Another v. Lala and NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 Others1 has awarded just and fair compensation which does not call for any modification.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and Another v. Lala and NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he seeks for allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

8. Per contra, Sri.Sanjay S.Katageri, learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that insofar as the negligence is concerned, the Tribunal has recorded a clear finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent and the said finding is based on the chargesheet filed by the jurisdictional Police, which does not call for interference.

He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal placing reliance on the Kishan Gopal's case referred supra is no doubt correct but however, it has failed to appreciate the fact that the Kishan Gopal's case referred supra is of the year 2014 and thereafter, much water is flown and the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of S Yallappa and others v.

The Managing Director, K.S.R.T.C., Bangalore in MFA No.3555/2015 has considered the income of the (2014) 1 SCC 244 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 deceased on the higher side, hence, he seeks to consider the same income and determine the compensation.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal filed by the appellants- claimants.
9. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously perused the material available on record.
10. It is not in dispute that in a road traffic accident dated 05.07.2015 Master Sheetal sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased was aged about 15 years at the time of the accident and was studying in 9th Standard.
Taking note of the same, the Tribunal has awarded compensation for the accidental death of the minor.

Material available on record indicates that the Jurisdictional Police after registering the crime have filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.KA-28/A-1971 which is insured with the appellant-Insurance Company.

The evidence of NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 PW2 who is claiming to be an eyewitness has deposed that the accident caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, however, in his cross- examination, a stray sentence has come where it is stated that the accident is caused due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
If the entire sentence of the cross-examination is read at para No.5, it gives a clear indication that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, contrary contention of the Insurance Company has no merit consideration.

The Tribunal taking note of the fact that the Police after completion of investigation, filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle held liability on the driver of the offending vehicle and no contrary evidence is produced by the Insurer to disbelieve the same.
Hence, the question of holding the rider of the motorcycle negligent partly would not arise.

Shri. Sudhakar S/O. Satappa Hosamani vs Shri Mahesh S/O. Adiveppa Gondali on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80674056/
4 11.

Insofar as non-possession of driving licence by the driver of the motorcycle is concerned, no attempt is NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 made by the Insurance Company to ascertain whether the driving licence was possessed by the rider of the motorcycle.

The insurer has not issued notice to the owner of the vehicle to produce driving licence, the insurer has filed only the application before the Tribunal for production of driving licence, that itself is not sufficient to come to the conclusion and to draw an adverse inference against the rider of the motorcycle that he was not holding driving licence at the time of accident.
It is well settled law that not holding of the licence ipso facto would not amount into negligence.
The insurer is required to prove the negligence of the rider of motorcycle independently.
Hence, to that extent, the contention of the Insurance Company does not hold any merit.

12. Admittedly, no chargesheet is filed against the rider of the motorcycle under Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, hence, the question holding that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess driving licence would not arise.
Yet another reason that no evidence is - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 available with regard to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, the said contention of the insurer is also rejected.

13. Insofar as entitlement of compensation is concerned, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in S Yallappa's case referred supra considering the Kishan Gopal's case referred supra has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.1,10,000/- per annum by adding future prospects of the deceased.

The relevant paragraphs of the aforesaid judgment read as follows:
"13.
The average inflation rate in India from 1992 to 2013 is 8.2% as per the data available on the internet.

Even by adopting a conservative approach, 7% simple interest is added to Rs.30,000.00, the notional annual income considered in the case of Kishan Gopal supra, for 21 years (1992 to 2013), the notional income per annum in 2013 would be Rs.74,100.00.
(Principal 30,000+Interest 44,100).

The same is rounded off to Rs.74,000/-.
14.
It is also required to be noticed that in Kishan Gopal's case supra, the future prospect was not taken into consideration.
In NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED V/S. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 the Apex Court provided for the addition of future prospects to the income of the deceased.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED V/S. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the said ratio, if 40% future prospects is added to the notional income of Rs.74,000.00, the notional income to assess `loss of dependency' would be Rs.1,03,600/-.
In Kishan Gopal's case supra, the deceased was aged 10 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 years.
In this case, the deceased was aged 17 years.

Considering the age of the deceased, this Court is of the view that notional income Shri.Sudhakar S/O. Satappa Hosamani vs Shri Mahesh S/O. Adiveppa Gondali on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80674056/
5 should be taken at Rs.1,10,000.00 per annum which is inclusive of future prospects.
The appropriate multiplier is 18 as the deceased was aged 17 years.
The `loss of dependency' would be 1,10,000x18/2=Rs.9,90,000.00.
Rs.40,000.00 each is to be awarded to the parents (Claimants No.1 and 2) towards the `loss of consortium'.
Rs.15,000.00 under each of the heads namely, loss of estate and funeral expenses is to be awarded.
Thus Rs.11,00,000.00 would be the compensation.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.5,40,000.00 as compensation to the parents of the boy aged 17 years who died in 2013.

The same would be grossly inadequate for the reasons assigned supra."
14.

In view of the above, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to assess the income of the deceased at Rs.1,10,000/- per annum which includes future prospects of the deceased.
15. The said judgment of the learned Single Judge has been challenged by the Corporation in SLP No.39089/2022 before the Hon'ble Apex Court.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has declined to interfere with the order of the learned Single Judge by order dated 05.01.2023.
In this case, the appropriate multiplier would be 18 as the deceased was 15 years old at the time of accident.

Thus, the appellants-claimants are entitled to modified compensation under the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.1,10,000 (Notional income p.a. inclusive of future prospects) x 18 (Multiplier) x 50% (Deduction) = Rs.9,90,000/-
17.
The claimants being the parents of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium.

The claimants are also entitled to Rs.15,000/-
under the heads of loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- under the head of transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
 Particulars Amount  (in Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 9,90,000/-
 Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Transportation of dead body and 15,000/-
 funeral expenses  - 13 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463
Shri.Sudhakar S/O. Satappa Hosamani vs Shri Mahesh S/O. Adiveppa Gondali

on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80674056/
6  Loss of consortium (Rs.40,000 X 2 80,000/-
 dependants)

Total 11,00,000/-
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- as against Rs.6,15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed and the appeal filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- as against Rs.6,15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11463 the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.

f) Registry to transmit amount in deposit, if any, along with records, if any, to the Tribunal,
forthwith.

g) Draw modified award accordingly.
Sd/-
(VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) JUDGE RH/ct-an Shri.Sudhakar S/O. Satappa Hosamani vs Shri Mahesh S/O. Adiveppa Gondali on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80674056/
